question.problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $\frac{1}{1-x},$ given by

$$
\frac{1}{1-x}=1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯\,,\,x\in (-1,1)
$$

using sigma notation.
question.worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =1 \\ {a}_{1} & =x \\ {a}_{2} & ={x}^{2} \\ {a}_{3} & ={x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & ={x}^{0} \\ {a}_{1} & ={x}^{1} \\ {a}_{2} & ={x}^{2} \\ {a}_{3} & ={x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}={x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1-x} & ={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{x}^{n}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
